rationale: The obligation asks whether the Pentachlorophenol row in Part I Section A for Outfall 001 establishes only monitoring and reporting without any enforceable numeric effluent discharge limit, as opposed to an applicable numeric limit or an inapplicable monitoring requirement. The packet shows the row places N/A in every mass- and concentration-limit cell (30-day average, daily max, and 7-day average columns) while specifying Report in the concentration 7-day average column together with 1/Quarter Grab sampling. That is affirmative permit text in the limits table itself, not inference from absence elsewhere. The same table contemporaneously lists pollutants with numeric limits (e.g., Cyanide with lbs/day and ug/L values), confirming that limit columns carry enforceable numeric values when applicable and that N/A marks non-applicability of numeric limits for this row. Report is a non-numeric reporting instruction, not a numeric discharge cap. The 1/Quarter Grab frequency is an active monitoring specification and the row carries no conditional footnote marker suggesting the requirement is out of effect. The authorization paragraph scopes these table entries to Outfall 001 discharges during the permit term. No packet evidence supports an applicable numeric limit for Pentachlorophenol in this row or that its monitoring requirement is not in effect; therefore the proposition is established and ACCEPT is warranted.
